assessments.label: A
assessments.reason: P/S fluid sensitivity is materially wrong: it says P is less sensitive to fluid disturbance and S is more sensitive to liquids, contrary to gold. Shale correction need is stated.

assessments.label: B
assessments.reason: Reverses the key physics by saying P is less sensitive and S more useful/sensitive for gas or fluids. Mentions shale correction only vaguely.

assessments.label: C
assessments.reason: Correctly explains P-wave fluid sensitivity, S-wave relative insensitivity to pore fluid, benefit of combining shear with compressional data, and need for shale/hydrocarbon corrections.

evidence_audit.relevance_reason: KB1 is the only retrieved item that materially relates to shear-wave use for fluid identification; the other retrieved items are generic sonic history/tool references or unrelated figure metadata and do not support the required claims about P/S pore-fluid sensitivity or shale correction.

citation_links.claim: P파의 민감도가 낮아 정확한 유체 식별이 어렵다.
citation_links.reason: KB3 says sonic responds primarily to porosity and is essentially independent of saturation; it does not support the claimed P-vs-S fluid sensitivity statement.

citation_links.claim: S파의 민감도가 높아 가스 함유층에서 유체 식별에 더 효과적일 수 있다.
citation_links.reason: KB1 says there is evidence shear transit time may be useful for fluid identification, but it does not support the stronger claim that S waves are more fluid-sensitive in gas zones.
